explain.say: Ask a grandparent what a bus ride cost when they were young. Much less! Inflation means prices in general rising over time, so each coin buys a little less. Look at the board: why does it happen? Four reasons are waiting.

explain.say: See the first reason: too much money. If lots of new money is printed but there are no extra goods, people chase the same goods with more money, and prices climb. Imagine everyone got double pocket money tomorrow. What would the shop do?

faq.a: Mainly too much money chasing too few goods, rising costs such as fuel and wages, very strong demand, and people expecting prices to rise.
Almost everything is moved by trucks, ships or planes, and factories and farms use energy. When fuel costs more, those costs get added to prices.
asks: Why does oil make things expensive?

faq.a: Hyperinflation is extremely fast inflation, often over 50 percent a month. Zimbabwe in 2008, Germany in 1923 and Venezuela in the late 2010s all suffered it, and money became almost worthless.

faq.q: What does a central bank do about inflation?
faq.a: It usually raises interest rates when inflation is too high, which makes borrowing dearer and slows spending. Many central banks aim for about 2 percent a year; India's targets 4 percent.

A little, steady inflation is normal and most economists think it is fine. High or unpredictable inflation hurts savers and people on fixed incomes, while falling prices, called deflation, can also cause problems.

facts: In November 2008, Zimbabwe's prices were doubling roughly every 25 hours.
The central banks of the UK, Japan and the euro area target 2% inflation; the Reserve Bank of India targets 4%.
